question.text: A single act of material misreporting by an SIA in Form 3.1 can, in principle, trigger which of the following parallel proceedings?

answer.text: SEBI Act adjudication / penalty, SIAB disciplinary proceedings, and civil / contractual claims by harmed investors - these can run in parallel subject to principles of natural justice and limitation.
Only SIAB disciplinary action - SEBI has no jurisdiction.
Only SEBI Act penalty - SIAB cannot act in parallel.
Only criminal prosecution under IPC, with no civil or administrative remedy.

explanation.text: The Logic: Conceptually, the Indian regulatory and disciplinary architecture permits parallel proceedings arising from the same act where the forums address distinct rights or interests: SEBI Act adjudication / penalty addresses market integrity, professional-body discipline (such as a SIAB-style mechanism) addresses fitness to practise, and civil / contractual claims by harmed investors address compensation. Each is subject to natural justice and applicable limitation periods. The Trap: Treating any one of SEBI, the professional body, or civil claims as having exclusive jurisdiction misreads the multi-track design. A criminal-only view ignores that administrative and civil remedies are typically the first-invoked layers. Note: The Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook (January 2026) supports the SIA code-of-conduct and confirms SEBI Act penalty / adjudication powers against defaulting intermediaries, but does not, on the pages reviewed, articulate a "SEBI adjudication + SIAB discipline + civil / contractual claims running in parallel" framework. The reasoning above reflects general Indian regulatory-procedure doctrine rather than a direct workbook citation.
